item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 24 March 2023, Tshisekedi reshuffled the government while retaining Prime Minister Sama Lukonde and appointing Jean-Pierre Bemba as Defense Minister, Vital Kamerhe as Economy Minister, Peter Kazadi as Interior Minister, and Antipas Mbusa Nyamwisi as Minister of State for Regional Integration; the cabinet also included ministers responsible for justice, finance, planning, infrastructure, health, education, social affairs, and other portfolios.","notes":["The excerpt identifies Mbusa Nyamwisi as Minister of State for Regional Integration, not simply Minister of Regional Cooperation."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Reuters reported that in the Lake Kivu methane auction, the government selected Canadian start-up Alfajiri despite an October 2022 government evaluation finding it lacked the required three years of financial records. A technical report initially scored Alfajiri last at 30.7/100, citing inadequate qualified staff, no feasibility study or timetable, and failure to address public-safety issues; a second version raised its score to 55.75 and placed it first. The hydrocarbons minister denied problems with the tender process, while Tshisekedi's office declined comment.","notes":["The excerpt supports the minister's denial of problems with the tender process, not the broader characterization that he denied wrongdoing."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"During a December 2023 election rally in Goma, Tshisekedi promised to continue fighting and eliminate M23, blamed Rwanda's Paul Kagame for backing the rebels, praised the army and Wazalendo fighters in the fight against armed groups, and called for UN peacekeepers to leave because he said their protection mission had failed. The article reported that M23 controlled large parts of the region, more than 120 armed groups were active in eastern Congo, and elections would not be held in some conflict-affected areas; the electoral commission had sought government help distributing ballots to insecure areas.","notes":["Corrected the unsupported wording error 'in the right against armed groups' to 'in the fight against armed groups.'"]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0009-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
